name: Should I hire a drywall installer or a licensed general contractor for water-damaged walls?
description: A general contractor is best when water damage involves structural framing, insulation replacement, plumbing leaks, or electrical concerns behind the wallboard.

mainEntity.name: Should I hire a drywall installer or a licensed general contractor for water-damaged walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both trades can install gypsum board, water intrusion creates distinct structural risks that benefit from a general contractor. A handyman can patch small, dry holes, but water damage often involves wet structural framing, saturated insulation, compromised electrical wiring, or hidden plumbing failures. A general contractor oversees the complete scope: identifying the underlying leak, coordinating structural drying, replacing insulation, ensuring structural studs are sound, and finishing the drywall to match existing architectural finishes across the space.
acceptedAnswer.description: A general contractor is best when water damage involves structural framing, insulation replacement, plumbing leaks, or electrical concerns behind the wallboard.
